text: Match the claim with appropriate evidence.

Formal checkpoints examine technical maturity, remaining risk and supporting records before major commitments. Proof could use tests, inspection or demonstration. Other methods include analysis, certification and description with supporting records. Requirement, design, readiness, verification and configuration reviews occur at different stages. Select the method that directly addresses the claim.

items: Name the claim being checked. You should see: One testable condition. If not: Return to the requirement if it is vague.
Choose suitable evidence. You should see: Inspection, analysis, demonstration, certification, description, or test. If not: Explain why the method can answer the claim.
Review the evidence at a suitable decision point. You should see: A recorded finding and remaining risk. If not: Do not treat an unresolved item as a pass.
Illustration: A visible identification mark can be inspected. A quantitative performance requirement generally calls for a measurement or a defensible analysis.

text: Make the verification approach depend on the question being answered, not on a favourite test method.
A signed review record cannot replace an absent technical check.
